column1: # The CI dependency graph (#1411). This file is the source; the workflow is checked
# against it, not the other way round.
#   stage <TAB> needs (comma-separated, `-` for none) <TAB> exports (`-` for nothing) <TAB> why
# Three rules are enforced by `.github/scripts/ci_graph_check.sh`:
#   1. A stage fixes nothing downstream by existing. `exports` is what it hands to a dependent:
#      an artifact, an output, or a compiled tree. A stage whose `exports` is `-` may not appear
#      in another stage's `needs` — a barrier is not a dependency, it is eleven minutes of wall
#      clock that produces nothing. `build` was exactly that: six `cargo check` legs plus a
#      `check_*.sh` loop, no `upload-artifact`, and five stages waiting on it (#1438).
#   2. `lint` is a leaf for every *stage* — now a consequence of rule 1, kept as its own error
#      because it cost seven subjects once. `build: needs: [workspace, lint]` skipped the build
#      and every stage downstream of it, so seven subjects never ran and the gate accused five
#      of them of failing (#1411).
#      `ci-report` and `gate` are the exception because they are not stages: their subject IS
#      every stage's result, so they must name every stage, `lint` included. The set is fixed in
#      the checker; a third aggregator is an error, not a convention.
#   3. An edge exists only when the upstream's result decides the downstream's subject. A
#      workspace that does not compile makes a test run meaningless; a lint finding does not.
# `portable`, `shell` and `wasm-gates` hang off nothing, because each has its own subject and
# none consumes a build artifact (#1410 is the same rule applied to one stage). `audit`, `docs`
# and `conformance` hang off nothing for the same reason: each compiles what it needs, and each
# waited eleven minutes for `build` to hand it nothing (#1438).
# stage
workspace

column1: lint
column4: style, architecture and the conventions suite over the tree — a leaf, deliberate
